title: Fix mis-scaled monetary amounts in UI with single conversion path + temporary compatibility layer

requirements.summary: Standardize frontend money display so backend amounts are converted exactly once (no double-scaling) across all money-rendering views and totals.
acceptanceCriteria: All monetary amounts shown in the UI (dashboards, group detail, contributions list, payout views, planned payments, etc.) are derived from a single shared conversion path and are not manually divided/multiplied elsewhere.
Totals are computed in the same unit as the raw backend values and only converted at the final render step (no mixed-unit arithmetic).
A regression check confirms the scenario in the uploaded screenshot (values like EUR 1.00 / EUR 2.00) displays correctly once the raw backend values are interpreted consistently.
No user-facing text is changed away from English.

file_operations.description: Create a centralized money conversion/rendering API (e.g., normalize-at-boundary + format-at-render) that ensures backend monetary amounts are converted exactly once and prevents component-local /100 scaling.
Refactor existing formatting helpers to delegate to the new shared conversion path (from frontend/src/lib/moneyModel.ts) so all UI formatting flows through one place.
Add/adjust cent-safe arithmetic helpers to work on normalized cents (bigint) without introducing any implicit /100 conversions during summation or percentage calculations.

Replace any direct numeric division (e.g., sum/100) and scattered centsToUnits calls with the shared money conversion/formatting functions to ensure totals + line items are rendered via a single conversion path.
Update money rendering and totals to use the shared money conversion/formatting functions so dashboard values cannot be double-scaled.
Ensure contributions totals and line-item amounts render using the shared conversion path; remove any manual /100 conversions or mixed-unit calculations.
Standardize dashboard money display (summaries, planned payments widgets, etc.) to use the shared conversion path and avoid any duplicate scaling.
Update payout totals and per-member payout amounts to use the shared conversion/formatting functions and keep all calculations in normalized cents until final render.
Update planned payment amount rendering to use the shared conversion/formatting functions and remove any local assumptions about stored units.
Update my planned payments amount rendering to use the shared conversion/formatting functions and ensure consistent scale across cards and badges.

requirements.summary: Add a temporary frontend money-model compatibility layer that deterministically normalizes legacy whole-unit records vs cent-stored records at query-consumption boundaries (no backend migration).
acceptanceCriteria: Frontend includes a single normalization function used at query-consumption boundaries (not scattered in UI components) that can handle legacy unit-stored values vs cent-stored values in a deterministic way.
The normalization layer includes safeguards to prevent double-scaling (e.g., values already in cents are not scaled again).
Normalization is applied consistently for contributions, expenses, revenues, group progress/financial summary, payouts, and planned payments wherever they are displayed or summed.
No backend state is altered; this is display/interpretation-only until backend truth is confirmed.

file_operations.description: Implement the money-model compatibility layer (single normalization function + model selection/override per group) with safeguards to prevent double-scaling and a deterministic selection strategy.

Apply money normalization at query-consumption boundaries (React Query hooks) so all fetched monetary fields (contributions/expenses/revenues/payouts/planned payments/group progress/financial summary/dashboard aggregates) are normalized once before reaching UI components.

Either remove the placeholder by wiring it to the new shared money-model normalization function or repurpose it as a thin wrapper around the centralized compatibility layer (to avoid scattered, one-off normalization logic).

Add an admin-only verification/debug section for money model selection and inspection that uses the authorization component to gate access (Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.) and allows deterministic per-group model override without changing backend state.

requirements.summary: Audit and update all money input flows so submitted values match the chosen money model consistently while preserving 2-decimal UX and validation.
acceptanceCriteria: All dialogs/forms that submit monetary values (e.g., add contribution/expense/revenue/planned payment) submit amounts in the backend-expected unit consistently (and do not rely on component-local scaling).
User inputs still accept up to 2 decimal places and show clear validation errors for invalid amounts.
Newly created records render in the UI with the same scale as existing records (no new mismatch introduced).

file_operations.description: Add a single submission-path helper for converting validated UI input into the backend-expected bigint amount according to the currently selected money model (ensuring inputs are never double-scaled and stay consistent with display normalization).
Update submission logic to use the shared money submission helper (rather than any implicit assumptions) while keeping the same 2-decimal input UX and existing validation behavior.
Update submission logic to use the shared money submission helper for amount -> backend value conversion; preserve current 2-decimal input UX and validation errors.
Update submission logic to use the shared money submission helper for amount conversion; keep 2-decimal UX and error handling.
Update planned payment submission logic to use the shared money submission helper and ensure newly created planned payments display with the same scale as existing records.
